- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–30% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 3–5 day peaks) — cap forecast at 2x the 14-day moving average after a spike.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is above 1.8, forecast should not exceed 2.2 unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles (e.g., 0.67, -0.33, 0.67), model tends to overshoot in the next cycle — dampen forecast by 15–25% in such alternating sentiment patterns.
- Model underestimates in high volatility periods (e.g., 2024-12-02) — if true outcome > 2x recent 7-day average, adjust forecast upward by 20–40% if sentiment is neutral or positive.
